yardstick.description: Every R_sig denominator is u_total(R) = sqrt(u_num^2 + granularity^2) (+ MC sigma only where the channel is nonlinear-flagged AND an MC run exists). No u_c exists anywhere (Phase 4 all-incomplete), so every verdict below is resolution-relative: it reports whether an effect clears, is marginal against, or is buried under the solver's own noise floor. It is NEVER a full prediction-uncertainty significance claim.
yardstick.mc_sigma: mc_sigma_absent on every row (no mc_sigma.json present at run time; driver never fails for missing MC)

bands.note: Order-of-magnitude reporting bands from spec §13.2's >>/approx/<< language; conventional-not-prescribed. No application decision may cite them without stating its own k.

limitations: u_c is null on every row: Phase 4 produced no human uncertainty values (§21 item 7 open), so no verdict above is a full prediction-uncertainty significance claim — all are resolution-relative against the solver's own noise floor.
mc_sigma_or_absent is mc_sigma_absent on every row: no mc_sigma.json was present at run time. Re-run with the MC stage's sigma file in LOB_VALIDATION_DIR to promote nonlinear channels.
Barometer and weather-station reference vectors are byte-identical duplicates (see duplicate_check); both kept, neither deduplicated — lob_env_test.cpp dedup stays deferred since Phase 3.
Single platform only: x86_64-linux, dev preset. Cross-platform noise guards are the floors.json ceilings, not re-measured here.
JOINT rows (spin-litz-vs-off, spin-boatright-vs-litz, jump-on-off) move named confounds together by construction; never cite them as isolated effects.
BOUND rows (tilted-vs-flat-datum, ceiling-clamp) are upper-bound/completion characterizations; never cite them as measured effects.

Two pre-registered expectations came back as findings, not confirmations: coriolis E/W elevation (Eotvos vertical sensitivity, R_sig to 264.9) and profile-vs-uniform deflection strength (distinguishable, not merely small). Both are recorded above, not smoothed over.
Long-range/field cells stay unclaimed (§21 item 11 open); the unclaimed list above renders the gap as data.
